title: Strings Without "ABC"
statement:
Count the strings of length `N` that use only the characters `'A'`, `'B'` and `'C'` and do **not** contain `"ABC"` as a contiguous substring.

Since the count can be very large, print it modulo `10^9 + 7`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of valid strings modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: There are 3^3 = 27 strings of length 3 and exactly one of them, "ABC", contains the forbidden substring, so 26 remain.
There are 81 strings of length 4. "ABC" can start at position 0 (3 strings: ABCA, ABCB, ABCC) or at position 1 (3 strings: AABC, BABC, CABC); these sets do not overlap, so 81 - 6 = 75.

hints: Build the string one character at a time. What do you need to remember about the end of the string to know whether the next character could complete "ABC"?
Only the longest suffix that is a prefix of "ABC" matters: it is empty, "A", or "AB". Keep a count of strings in each of these three states.
From each state, work out where each of the three next characters leads. The only forbidden move is appending 'C' to a string ending in "AB". Remember to take everything modulo 10^9 + 7.
